answer: No seat can claim an orchard it does not farm. Each parcel holds a registered deed and a harvest notary, and its crop leaves under a sealed manifest that makes a voyage to a bonded warehouse; there the lot is sampled and matched against the parcel's own velvet bloom season, measured from orbit. Two seats tied to one parcel share a single bloom record and collide, so a k-seat farm must lease k separate parcels, each paying its own rent, notary, sampling, and freight. Paperwork is cheap to copy; a second harvest is not.
